index.exportDatabaseDesc: Click to download a .db file containing a backup of your current database to your device.
index.importDatabaseDesc: Click to select and upload a .db file from your device to restore your database from a backup.
index.importDatabaseSuccess: The database has been successfully imported.
index.importDatabaseError: An error occurred while importing the database.
index.backupPostgresNote: This panel runs on PostgreSQL. Back Up downloads a pg_dump archive (.dump) and Restore loads it back with pg_restore. The server needs the PostgreSQL client tools (pg_dump and pg_restore) installed.
index.exportDatabasePgDesc: Click to download a PostgreSQL dump (.dump) of your current database to your device.
index.importDatabasePgDesc: Click to select and upload a .dump file to restore your PostgreSQL database. This replaces all current data.

inbounds.deleteConfirmContent: This removes the inbound and all its clients. This cannot be undone.
inbounds.resetConfirmContent: Resets up/down counters to 0 for this inbound.
inbounds.bulkDeleteConfirmContent: This removes the selected inbounds and all their clients. This cannot be undone.
inbounds.cloneConfirmContent: Creates a copy with a new port and an empty client list.
inbounds.attachClientsDesc: Attaches the same {count} clients (same UUID/password and shared traffic) to the selected inbound(s). They stay on this inbound too.
inbounds.attachClientsNoTargets: No other compatible inbounds available to attach to.
inbounds.attachExistingDesc: Attaches existing clients ({count} available) to this inbound — same UUID/password and shared traffic. Clients already on it are skipped.
inbounds.attachExistingNoClients: No clients exist yet. Create clients first, then attach them here.
inbounds.detachClientsDesc: Removes the selected client(s) from this inbound only. Client records themselves are kept (use Delete to remove fully). Source has {count} clients in total.
inbounds.resetTrafficContent: Are you sure you want to reset traffic?
inbounds.resetAllTrafficContent: Are you sure you want to reset the traffic of all inbounds?

toasts.savedNodeOfflineWillSync: Saved locally. A backing node is offline or disabled — the change will sync once it reconnects.

clients.emailInvalidChars: Email cannot contain spaces, '/', '\', or control characters
clients.subIdInvalidChars: Subscription ID cannot contain spaces, '/', '\', or control characters
clients.noConnectionUri: No entrypoints — assign a group with entrypoints first.
clients.resetNotPossible: Attach this client to an inbound first.
clients.deleteConfirmContent: This removes the client from every attached inbound and drops its traffic record. This cannot be undone.
clients.bulkAdjustNothing: Set days or traffic before applying.

groups.deleteConfirmContent: This removes the group and clears its label from {count} client(s). The clients themselves are not deleted.

nodes.name: Name
nodes.deleteConfirmContent: This stops monitoring the node. The remote panel itself is unaffected.

toasts.fillRequired: Name, address, port and API token are required

settings.dnsPrimaryDesc: Where nodes forward whatever the cache does not hold. An IPv6 address is fine — the resolver still asks it for A records.
settings.dnsSecondaryDesc: Asked whenever the first one stays silent.
settings.dnsCacheDesc: How many names a node keeps in memory. The cache is shared by every client on it.
settings.dnsTtlDesc: Lower and upper bound on how long an answer lives in the cache.
settings.dnsStaleDesc: A stale answer goes out at once and is refreshed in the background. 0 turns it off.
settings.dnsNoRecords: No records — everything goes to the upstreams.
settings.restartingDesc: Applying your changes — the panel will be back in a moment.
settings.pageSizeDesc: Define page size for inbounds table. (0 = disable)
settings.mtuDesc: Largest packet the node carries for a client.
settings.statsSecondsDesc: How often a node samples its datapath counters. (0 = disable, unit: second)
settings.datepickerDescription: Scheduled tasks will run based on this calendar.
settings.expireTimeDiffDesc: Get notified about expiration date when reaching this threshold. (unit: day)
settings.trafficDiffDesc: Get notified about traffic cap when reaching this threshold. (unit: GB)
settings.timeZoneDesc: Scheduled tasks will run based on this time zone.
settings.poolDesc: Range each connected client is given an address from.
settings.brutalDesc: Send at this many Mbit/s regardless of loss — set it below the real line. Zero hands the pacing to cubic, which backs off on loss instead.
settings.maxStreamsDesc: How many flows one connection may hold open at once. A browser alone takes hundreds, and on an exit node every client transits through a single connection. Raise it before the client count does.
settings.streamWindowDesc: Starting and largest receive window of one flow, in kilobytes. Above the bandwidth-delay product it only buys latency.
settings.connWindowDesc: Starting and largest receive window shared by all flows of one client, in kilobytes.
settings.socketBufferDesc: Kilobytes the node asks the kernel for on the listening socket. The kernel caps it at net.core.rmem_max.
settings.idleDesc: Seconds a silent connection is held, and how often it is pinged to stay open through NAT.

publish.title: Publish to the network
publish.skippedHint: Nodes without a control channel are skipped — they pick this revision up when they reconnect.

import.title: Paste your link
import.subtitle: One link is the whole setup — no account, no password.
import.hint: Ctrl+V anywhere on this page works too.
import.clipboardDenied: The browser would not hand over the clipboard — paste it instead.

connect.exitRefused: This subscription does not allow exit nodes.

routing.noRules: No rules. Every process follows the default above.
routing.everythingElseDesc: Processes with no rule, plus traffic the system sends on its own behalf — that has no process to attribute it to.

roleDesc.direct: Straight out of this machine. Never enters the tunnel.
roleDesc.tunnel: Into the tunnel. Whether it leaves through an exit node follows the +egress switch on Connect.
roleDesc.egress: Into the tunnel and out through an exit node, whatever the switch says.
roleDesc.noEgress: Into the tunnel and out at the entry node, whatever the switch says.

routing.newFlowsNote: Rules apply to new connections. Anything already open finishes on the route it started on — moving a live connection would change the address the far end sees and it would drop the session.
routing.matchNote: A rule picked from a running process matches that exact file. One typed by name matches any process called that, wherever it was started from.
routing.searchProcess: Search running processes, or type a name
routing.noProcesses: Nothing is running with an open connection.
routing.byNameHint: Add by name — matches any process called this
routing.restartNeeded: Rules are waiting for a reconnect
routing.restartNeededDesc: Android fixes per-app rules when the tunnel is built, so these land the next time it comes up.
routing.restartNeededIdle: Android fixes per-app rules when the tunnel is built, so these land when you connect.
routing.resetRulesDesc: Removes every rule and puts all traffic back on the default. The tunnel stays up.

settings.sitesNote: Read from the local resolver. This never leaves the machine and is cleared by either reset.
settings.refreshIntervalDesc: How often to fetch the subscription, in minutes. 1 to 1440.
settings.autostartBehaviourDesc: What happens when the system starts the client.
settings.manualBehaviourDesc: What happens when you launch it yourself.
settings.resetDataDesc: Settings and the resolver history go back to defaults. The subscription is kept and the tunnel is not interrupted.
settings.resetAllDesc: Settings and the imported link are both dropped. The next start opens the import screen again.

history.empty: Nothing recorded yet — the tunnel has to be up for a moment first.
